messages:
sam_product: quick thread — we need to lock down the "relevancy" endpoint behavior for launch. customers keep asking about: top_k semantics, score normalization, truncation rules, and supported input shapes. can we get proposals + launch guardrails by EOD?

jules_eng: ok sketched some options below. TL;DR: default top_k=5, allow up to 100, add optional `normalize_scores` flag, and define truncation priority (drop least-likely tokens from candidates).

tess_ml: +1 on optional normalization. computing a softmax across variable candidate sets has cost and numeric edgecases. suggest server-side stable softmax and an opt-out param. also: define whether scores are comparable across requests/models. they won't be without calibration.

omar_sre: latency guardrails: current infra 95p token-latency baseline for rerank is ~45ms per candidate on p4. rough rule: adding normalization should not increase p95 by >15%. if customers need cross-model comparable scores, that's a separate offline calibration job.

mike_pm: customers want two things: (1) simplicity for basic use (give top-k candidates + return scores normalized 0-1) and (2) advanced control for platforms (pass many candidates, get raw logits). propose we support both via params: `top_k`, `max_candidates`, `normalize_scores` (bool), `return_raw_scores` (bool).

claire_design: API UX notes: prefer `top_k` to control returned results, `max_candidates` to limit server-side candidate ingest. responses should include `ranking_reason` (enum) for common behaviors. Also include explicit `truncation` flag in response when any input was truncated so users can instrument. sample response shape idea in docs section.

nora_data: scoring normalization tradeoff — if we normalize per-request, distributions differ by candidate pool size. that will change logging/metrics. we should add a field `score_basis` that says "per-request-softmax" vs "raw-logits" vs "calibrated". important for later metrics and evals.

jules_eng: implementation notes: candidate input formats to support: (A) single request: `{ query: "q", candidates: [{id, text, metadata}] }` (B) streaming/batched candidates via multipart upload for huge corpora. truncation rules: we can choose 1) truncate candidate text from tail, 2) truncate by token budget globally (prefer drop candidates with lowest pre-score), or 3) reject with 413 if payload > limit. my preference: global token budget + best-effort preserve top candidates by short-circuiting a cheap approximate scorer.

tess_ml: cheap approximate scorer idea: use a lightweight vector dot on embeddings to pre-filter heavy candidates. that gives deterministic ordering for truncation. need to document that pre-filter may change final top_k in rare edgecases.

mike_pm: launch criteria proposal: 1) API stable shape: supports `top_k`, `normalize_scores`, `return_raw_scores`, `max_candidates` and `score_basis` in response. 2) Perf: p95 latency increase < 15% vs baseline when `normalize_scores=true` for up to 50 candidates. 3) Docs + SDK examples for node/python. 4) 2 pilot customers validated. 5) Backwards-compatible default (normalize_scores=false by default).

omar_sre: ops checklist: rate limit per-candidate counts, hard payload size (JSON bytes) limit, circuit-breaker when candidate count causes OOM. add metrics: candidates_ingested, truncated_count, normalization_time_ms.

claire_design: small sample snippet for docs (how to call):
```
POST /v1/relevancy
{
  "query": "How to reset password",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "Reset password via settings"},
    {"id": "c2", "text": "Forgot password link"}
  ],
  "top_k": 3,
  "normalize_scores": true
}
```

jules_eng: edgecases: tied scores (identical logits) — we should have deterministic tie-breaker: candidate id lexicographic. empty candidate array => 400. `top_k` > `candidates.length` => pad with empty entries? prefer returning fewer results and `returned_k` field.

nora_data: evaluation hooks: provide optional `gold_label` in request for internal evals and attach `eval_id` in response. don't leak that into logs by default.

mike_pm: prioritization: must-have for initial GA: top_k param, raw scores, max_candidates limit, clear truncation flag and docs. nice-to-have: streaming candidate ingest, server-side calibration, `ranking_reason` detailed enum.

sam_product: decision summary so far (draft):
- default behavior: `top_k=5`, `normalize_scores=false` (backwards compat)
- expose params: `top_k`, `max_candidates`, `normalize_scores`, `return_raw_scores`
- response: include `scores[]`, `score_basis`, `returned_k`, `truncated: true|false` and `truncation_reason` if true
- truncation policy v1: global token budget (e.g., 64k tokens) -> if exceeded, run cheap pre-filter (embedding dot) and drop lowest pre-score candidates, set `truncated=true`
- tie-break: deterministic by ID lexicographic
- launch guards: perf p95 < baseline *1.15 (for up to 50 candidates), docs + SDKs, 2 pilot customers signed off

sam_product: action items: @jules_eng prototype pre-filter + truncation logic, @tess_ml run normalization perf numbers, @omar_sre add candidate metrics + circuit breakers, @mike_pm draft customer pilot plan. please ack and estimate EOD. :white_check_mark:

jules_eng: ack — I'll prototype today. estimate: 2-3 engineer-days for prototype + perf harness.

tess_ml: ack — will run numbers, need access to p4 cluster for perf.

omar_sre: ack — I'll add metrics + a safety limit in config.

mike_pm: ack — will prepare pilot outreach and docs skeleton.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: feature/exp-relevancy-truncation -> staging at 2026-03-15T18:12:00Z :rocket:

sam_product: thanks all. will consolidate into a spec PR tomorrow. :smile:
